leads.title: Lockheed CL-400 reconnaissance aircraft using liquid hydrogen as fuel (three-view drawing with data block)
leads.shows: Front, top and side views of the Lockheed CL-400 Suntan design with its data block (T.O.G.W. 69,955 lb, fuel load 21,440 lb, crew 2, two 304-2 engines, 164 ft 10 in long, 83 ft 9 in span). Caption: "Fig. 34. Lockheed CL-400 reconnaissance aircraft using liquid hydrogen as fuel, ca. 1955." Source given as Ben R. Rich, "Lockheed CL-400 Liquid Hydrogen-Fueled Mach 2.5 Reconnaissance Vehicle", symposium on hydrogen-fueled aircraft, NASA Langley Research Center, 15-16 May 1973.
leads.creator: Lockheed Aircraft Corporation (via Ben R. Rich, 1973 paper); reproduced in John L. Sloop, NASA SP-4404
leads.rights_evidence: SP-4404 web edition caption (Wayback capture of http://history.nasa.gov/SP-4404/ch8-3.htm, 2002) credits the figure to Ben R. Rich's 1973 Lockheed paper. NTRS record 19790008823 marks the book "GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED" (Public Use Permitted), but that covers NASA's text; the drawing is Lockheed work, so under the project rule it is not tier A.
leads.notes: Ask Lockheed Martin (Skunk Works / corporate communications) for permission to host, or accept the NASA public-use determination as a risk decision. Shows the CL-400 that the 18 January 1956 Putt meeting set in motion; no photograph of the meeting itself is known. Fig. 35 on the same page is the CL-400 mission profile (same source, same rights). Page images checked by thumbnail. URLs verified HTTP 200 (206 for ranged file requests) on 2026-10-05. Wayback image is 200; NASA PDF 200 (ranged).

leads.title: Johnson's A-1 sketches, 23 April and 26 June 1958
leads.shows: Kelly Johnson's pencil sketches of the A-1 (Archangel 1): front and plan views dated 23 April 1958 and plan and side views dated 26 June 1958. CIA caption: "A sampling of Johnson's drawings, including the A-1, A-3, and Convair FISH".
leads.creator: Clarence L. 'Kelly' Johnson, Lockheed Aircraft Corporation (released by CIA)
leads.rights_evidence: Drawn by Clarence L. 'Kelly' Johnson of Lockheed Aircraft Corporation (a contractor, not a federal employee). CIA publishes it with no copyright notice or credit, and the monograph's acknowledgements say: "I also am grateful for historical material provided by the Lockheed Martin Corporation and the A-12 program veterans, the Roadrunners" (Robarge, Archangel, 2012, p. iii). Under the project rule this is tier D: ask Lockheed Martin Corporation (Skunk Works / corporate communications) or decide to rely on the CIA public-domain statement as a documented risk. CIA Site Policies, Copyright Notice: "Unless a copyright is indicated, information on our website is in the public domain and may be reproduced, published or otherwise used without our permission. We request only that our Agency be cited as the source of the information and that any photo credits or bylines be similarly credited to the photographer or author or our Agency, as appropriate." (https://www.cia.gov/site-policies/, read 2026-10-05)
leads.notes: Best visual for the event: the 23 April 1958 sketch is the first Archangel drawing. Same drawings appear with date labels on p. 2 of the CIA monograph PDF (https://www.cia.gov/resources/csi/static/b45f5f8f5e4937963d9e9931313d84a4/Archangel-CIAs-Supersonic-A-12-Reconnaissance-Aircraft.pdf). No higher-resolution master found; Johnson's original log is not public. Page that hosted it: the 2007 CIA web edition 'Lockheed' sidebar (Wayback). leads.title: A-12 60-6924 lifting off with landing gear down (Lou Schalk)
leads.shows: The first A-12 just after lift-off, seen from below with the main gear still down, mountains on the horizon. Captioned by CIA as the A-12's 'second flight ever'.
leads.creator: Unknown; probably Lockheed company photography (contributed by Lockheed to Roadrunners Internationale)
leads.rights_evidence: Commons tags it {{PD-USGov-DoD}} but gives the source as the 'Area 51' book promotional site, "credited to CIA/Roadrunners Internationale"; the Roadrunners copy sits in a gallery headed "A-12 Planes Photos Contributed by Lockheed" (footer: "Copyright 2001- [year] , Dreamland Resort . All rights reserved."); Lockheed Martin publishes it on its own history site. CIA also publishes the frame with no credit (2007 web edition ch3_2.jpg; Archangel 2012 p.22) under its policy: "Unless a copyright is indicated, information on our website is in the public domain" (https://www.cia.gov/site-policies/).
leads.notes: Dating conflict: CIA captions this frame "A rare photo of an airborne A-12 with landing gear visible, here on its second flight ever" (2007 web edition, full-stress-testing.html, ch3_2.jpg 576x264; 2012 Archangel PDF p.22, 576x271, darker crop); Lockheed Martin's centennial page dates it 26 April 1962 as the maiden flight (per the Commons description); Roadrunners labels it "A-12 Article 924 Lou Schalk's 2d flight - Groom Lake 5/4/62"; habu.org says 30 April 1962. Gear down fits the 26 April flight, which Robarge says Schalk flew 'with the landing gear down, just in case', and counting the 25 April hop it was the aircraft's second flight; so 26 April 1962 is best supported, but say 'April or May 1962' unless the site settles it. Aircraft is 60-6924 (Article 121), the only A-12 flying before late June 1962. Rights decision for the site: either rely on CIA's public-domain statement for its own published copy (and treat as tier A at that copy's size) or ask Lockheed Martin for the original. CIA copy URL: https://web.archive.org/web/20071010034935id_/https://www.cia.gov/library/center-for-the-study-of-intelligence/csi-publications/books-and-monographs/a-12/images-and-thumbnails/ch3_2.jpg

leads.title: A-12 - Q1 - Article 924 at Area 51 on its very first landing

leads.creator: Lockheed (contributed to Roadrunners Internationale); photographer not named
leads.rights_evidence: Roadrunners Internationale gallery page https://roadrunnersinternationale.com/photos_a12_planes.html is headed "A-12 Planes Photos Contributed by Lockheed"; page footer: "Copyright 2001- [current year] , Dreamland Resort . All rights reserved." No licence is given for the image files.
leads.notes: If the caption is right this is the end of Schalk's unannounced hop of 25 April 1962, when he put the aircraft down on the lakebed beyond the runway; the photo alone cannot confirm runway or lakebed. Small copy; ask Lockheed Martin for the original and Roadrunners for the scan.

leads.title: Remnants of the crashed A-12 near Wendover, Utah, 1963
leads.shows: NatGeo caption: "Remnants of a crashed A-12 spy plane, including two engines and the shattered rear fuselage, litter the ground near Wendover, Utah, in a 1963 picture recently declassified by the CIA and published here for the first time." (original punctuation uses dashes)
leads.creator: Central Intelligence Agency (as credited: "Photograph from CIA via Pangloss Films")
leads.rights_evidence: NatGeo News gallery 'Area 51 Pictures: Secret Plane Crash Revealed', 20 May 2011, credit on each crash photo: "Photograph from CIA via Pangloss Films"; page footer "(c) 1996-2011 National Geographic Society". CIA historian David Robarge is quoted there: "the photos of the 1963 crash no longer are [sensitive], and so they were declassified and released."
leads.notes: The underlying photographs are CIA records declassified in 2011 and very probably US government works, so the right route to a hostable tier A copy is to request the originals from CIA (Office of Public Affairs or the Information Management Services FOIA office); no copy was found in the reading room mirror. Five CIA crash photos are in the gallery: wreckage (35808), aerial view of the recovery camp (35800_600x450), heavy equipment (35807), crane loading debris on a flatbed (35802), wreckage under tarps (35806); all captured by the Wayback Machine at 600x450. The gallery's radar-pylon photo is credited to Roadrunners, not CIA. Related video: NatGeo 'Area 51 Declassified' (2011) excerpts with Ken Collins describing the ejection, catalog nvahof-natgeo-area-51-declassified-excerpts (tier C).

The person is identified by context (Hayden gave the commemorative remarks per the programme), not by a caption. Hostable alternative: candidate 3 (CIA photo of 60-6931 on its pylons, 15 September 2008, public domain, 4368x2912).

leads.title: A-12 Aircraft Presentation Ceremony programme (scan)
leads.shows: CIA programme card: "A-12 Aircraft Presentation Ceremony, Wednesday, 19 September 2007, 2:00 p.m." Welcoming remarks Toni Hiley (Agency Museum Director), presentation of colours, national anthem, film "Codename: OXCART", commemorative remarks by General Michael V. Hayden, USAF, Director, CIA, and unveiling of an A-12 painting; CIA seal and 60th anniversary logo.
leads.creator: Central Intelligence Agency (programme); scan by Roadrunners Internationale
leads.rights_evidence: Same site notice as above. The programme text and design appear to be CIA work (CIA seal, Agency 60th anniversary mark), which would make the content itself U.S. government work, but the copy found is the Roadrunners scan.
leads.notes: Exact primary document for the event and it settles the date. Either obtain permission for the scan or ask CIA's museum for its own copy, which would be tier A.
